assets: cluster-wide operator privileges (namespace/pod/exec wildcards held by the controller-manager ServiceAccount)
tenant workspace namespaces, workloads, PVCs, and model inventories
Ollama compute and storage (GPU/CPU quotas, 20Gi model PVC)
Open WebUI chat data, accounts, and signing key
system MySQL database deployed by the default overlay
operator runtime memory and mounted ServiceAccount token
assumptions: no out-of-repo admission webhook, policy engine, or service mesh is present; the webhook server in cmd/main.go registers no handlers
workspace namespaces are DNS-1123-label names; the API server rejects invalid namespace names, which constrains label/host syntax injection but not namespace selection
an ingress controller and wildcard DNS are deployment prerequisites for external exposure of the generated Ingresses
attackerCapabilities: create/update/delete AIChatWorkspace CRs in a namespace they control (namespaced privilege, no cluster rights)
reach Ingress-exposed workspace hosts once an ingress controller is deployed
reach any ClusterIP service in the cluster network (no NetworkPolicies applied by default)
same-pod position via sidecar, ephemeral debug container, or pods/exec/port-forward
commit or review supply-chain material in the public repository
securityObjectives: a namespaced CR author must only affect namespaces and resources the operator derives from their own CR
the operator must not delete or mutate namespaces it did not create for that CR
workspace services (Ollama, Open WebUI) must not be reachable by unauthenticated network users by default
workloads and the manager must run with least privilege
no working credentials may be published in the repository and deployed by default
threatModel.summary: A Go Kubernetes operator (Kubebuilder) reconciles the namespaced AIChatWorkspace custom resource into a per-workspace namespace running Ollama and Open WebUI with Services and Ingresses. The operator runs with one cluster-wide ServiceAccount whose ClusterRole grants wildcard verbs over namespaces, pods, pods/exec, workloads, services, PVCs, service accounts, resource quotas, ingresses, and KEDA HTTPScaledObjects. The primary trust boundary is the AIChatWorkspace CR: a cluster user with only namespaced rights on that CR (the shipped aichatworkspace-editor-role is designed for exactly this) can supply spec.workspaceName, spec.models, and spec.patterns, which the cluster-privileged operator consumes with no admission or ownership validation. Secondary boundaries: network users reaching the operator-created Ingresses that expose the unauthenticated Ollama API and Open WebUI; the operator pod's localhost debug listener; in-cluster workloads reaching the default-deployed MySQL; and the build/devcontainer supply chain.
trustBoundaries: AIChatWorkspace CR (namespaced user input) -> cluster-privileged operator reconcile path
external network via Ingress -> workspace Ollama API and Open WebUI
manager pod network namespace (sidecar/same-pod) -> localhost:6060 debug mux
operator system namespace ConfigMap -> workspace container image selection
repo/CI supply chain -> published operator image and dev workstations
